tax_report.title: Annual tax report
tax_report.empty: No sales, dividends or fees recorded yet.
tax_report.two_month_explainer: Two-month rule (Spanish income tax act, art. 33.5.f): if you buy the same security (same ISIN) in the two months before or after a sale at a loss, that loss is not included that year; it is included when you definitively sell the repurchased shares. "Computable losses" already excludes the deferred ones and the net subtracts those included this year.
tax_report.no_isin_warning: {{count}} transaction(s) without ISIN: the two-month rule is applied by name and may be wrong (two products with the same name, or one with two names). Review those sales.
tax_report.no_isin_note: No ISIN: the two-month rule is applied by name and may be wrong (no. of transactions)
tax_report.partial_history_note: Only the shares with a purchase in the history are counted; those without one are NOT in the totals (see "Shares sold without cost")
tax_report.partial_history_row: {{shares}} share(s) without cost, left out of the totals
tax_report.partial_history_warning: {{count}} sale(s) with shares that have no purchase in the history. For each one, only the part with a purchase is counted; the shares in the "Shares sold without cost" table and their transfer value are NOT in the totals. Add the missing purchase (import your broker's full history) to include them.
tax_report.partial_history_section: Shares sold without cost (left out of the totals)
tax_report.pending_section: Pending deferred losses (as of the latest data)
tax_report.fees_note: Buy and sell commissions are already INSIDE the acquisition and transfer values (Spanish income tax act, art. 35), each at the exchange rate of its date. "Other fees" are the ones not tied to a trade (connectivity, custody…): they are not included in those values and do not reduce the gain or loss.
tax_report.unreliable_warning: {{count}} sale(s) without buy history for ANY of the shares sold: with no acquisition cost their P&L can't be computed, so they are NOT included in the totals (marked with ⚠ in the table). Import your broker's full history.
tax_report.loading_rates: Loading the exchange rate of each transaction's date…
tax_report.rates_error: Historical exchange rates could not be loaded. Foreign-currency transactions are left out of the totals until you reopen the report.
tax_report.missing_fx_warning: {{count}} foreign-currency transaction(s) without an exchange rate for their date: they are NOT included in the totals (we never use today's rate). They are listed under "No exchange rate" in the CSV.
tax_report.missing_fx_section: No exchange rate (left out of the totals)
tax_report.missing_fx_note: Not counted: no exchange rate for its date
tax_report.source_historical: Historical (same day or previous business day)
tax_report.reason_no_rate: No rate for that date or the 7 previous days
tax_report.disclaimer: Indicative report built with the FIFO method on your imported data. Each foreign-currency amount is converted at the exchange rate of its transaction date (or the previous business day): for a sale, the transfer value at the sale-date rate and the acquisition value at the rate of each purchase date, as the Spanish tax agency requires. The two-month rule is applied by ISIN, whatever the market or trading currency (so it may differ from the brokers screen, which splits by currency). Buy commissions add to the acquisition value and sell commissions reduce the transfer value; standalone fees are listed separately under "Other fees". Dividends are shown as your broker records them: on DEGIRO and IBKR they are the GROSS amount and withholding appears separately under "Withholding tax" (declare the gross amount and deduct the withholding). If your broker pays dividends already net, there will be no separate withholding. This is not tax advice — check your broker's tax certificates before filing.

portfolio_score.empty_hint: Import a CSV or add positions in Portfolio to see your score.
portfolio_score.info_diversification: Uses the HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index): sums the square of each position's weight (value / total portfolio). HHI = 1 means everything is in one asset → 0 pts. The more weight is spread across positions, the lower HHI is and the higher the score. 10 equal positions → HHI = 0.10 → 22.5 pts. 1 single position → HHI = 1 → 0 pts.
portfolio_score.info_performance: Maps your total ROI (unrealised + realised gain + dividends − fees, over historical invested capital) onto a −30% to +30% scale. A 0% ROI gives 12.5 pts; +30% or above gives the full 25 pts.
portfolio_score.info_costs: Calculates the fee ratio: total fees / invested capital × 100. Below 0.5% earns the full 20 pts. Each additional 1% of ratio deducts 10 pts. Above 2% the score is 0.
portfolio_score.info_liquidity: Measures the % of cash relative to total portfolio value. The optimal range is 5–15% (max 15 pts). Below 5% leaves no buffer to act. Above 40% means too much idle capital (minimum 2 pts).

cartera.metric_market_formula: Σ (Quantity × Current Market Price) — invested assets only
cartera.metric_market_desc: What your assets are worth right now at market price, excluding cash. The "Net worth" below does add cash (or subtracts it, if you use margin). For funds, the price is their latest published NAV, which can be 1-2 days old.
cartera.metric_gain_desc: Your total profit or loss. "Unrealised (today)" is the difference between the current market value and the cost of your open positions. The other three components are historical cumulative totals since the first operation.
cartera.metric_twr_formula: Chained product of daily returns: ∏(1 + rᵢ) − 1
cartera.metric_twr_desc: Industry standard. Measures how your investments did removing the effect of WHEN and HOW MUCH you contributed: it chains each day's return, so adding or withdrawing money does not move it. It counts price and currency; it does NOT include dividends or fees (those are in Total Gain). It is the figure to compare yourself with the S&P 500 or other indices. "Adjusted" means exactly that: adjusted for your contributions.
cartera.metric_cagr_window: Measured from your first purchase, {{date}} — {{years}} years invested. Money sitting in cash before that date does not count.
cartera.metric_cagr_desc: Normalises the total return to its annual equivalent using TWR (time-weighted return), immune to the timing of your contributions. Years are counted from your FIRST INVESTED DAY — not from the first movement on the account — so cash sitting idle before your first purchase does not drag the figure down. Note it is a COMPOUND rate, not an average: +60% over two years is not +30% a year but +26.5%, because the second year grows on top of the first. Only meaningful with more than 6 months invested.
cartera.metric_latent_formula: Market value − FIFO cost of open positions
cartera.metric_latent_desc: The profit or loss you have right now on your open positions, over what you paid for them. It only becomes real if you sell.
cartera.metric_realized_formula: Σ (Sale amount − FIFO cost of what was sold)
cartera.metric_realized_desc: What you have already gained or lost by selling, fully or partly. Cost is FIFO: the first shares you bought are the first ones sold. Sale fees are not deducted here; they are in Fees.
cartera.metric_dividends_desc: Total dividends received from what you hold or have held, as your broker records them. DEGIRO and IBKR record withholding as a separate line: here you see the GROSS amount and the withholding counts in Fees. With brokers that pay the dividend already net, it is the net amount.
cartera.metric_commissions_formula: Σ Trade fees + broker charges (custody, FX, taxes)
cartera.metric_commissions_desc: Everything your brokers charged you: per-order fees, custody, FX and any taxes or withholding the statement records as a charge. DEGIRO and IBKR trade fees are invoiced in euros; the rest in their own currency.
cartera.metric_roi_current_desc: The return on what you hold now: unrealised gain over what you paid for those positions (FIFO cost). It does not count past sales, dividends or fees. Unlike TWR, it DOES depend on when you contributed: a recent purchase has not had time to grow yet and pulls the percentage down. That is why it can be much lower than TWR without anything being wrong.

portfolio_growth.label: Investment Evolution
portfolio_growth.title: Portfolio Return
portfolio_growth.no_data: Not enough data to generate the evolution chart.
portfolio_growth.twr_desc: The industry standard (Bloomberg, IBKR, Fidelity) for measuring investment decisions. Unaffected by cash flows — each cash flow splits the period into independent sub-periods.
portfolio_growth.roi_actual_desc: Return relative to the cost of currently open positions. When you sell, the cost of those shares disappears from the denominator — the percentage reflects only what you hold today. It is the SAME number as the "Current portfolio ROI" chip on the brokers screen: if they ever disagree, one of them is using incomplete market data.
portfolio_growth.roi_formula: ROI = (Market Value − Open Cost) / Open Cost
portfolio_growth.roi_note: The percentage comes from the TWO figures shown above — live market value ÷ invested capital — so it is exactly the same "Current portfolio ROI" the brokers screen shows. It is only offered over the full range (ALL), and that is deliberate: over a shorter stretch the line rebases to 0% on its first date, and then it stops measuring a return and starts measuring how much your ROI CHANGED. A contribution adds the same euros to both value and cost, so it drags that ratio towards 0% however well the market does — you can make money and still see red. For the return over a stretch, the metric is TTWROR, which is immune to when the money went in.
portfolio_growth.sp500_desc: Available in TWR mode. Compares whether your portfolio outperforms the benchmark over the same period.
portfolio_growth.beta_desc: Realized gains/losses correspond to the gains or losses experienced after selling an asset. They represent the difference between the sale price and the original purchase price. The relative return is calculated by dividing the sum of gains/losses by the sum of purchase prices of the sold assets.
portfolio_growth.beta_formula: Beta ROI = Σ(Sale Price − Purchase Price) / Σ(Purchase Price of sold) × 100
portfolio_growth.beta_note: Only reflects completed (sold) trades. Does not include open positions or unrealized gains.
portfolio_growth.ttwror_desc: Absolute GIPS standard. Subdivides periods daily, completely isolating daily cash inflows and withdrawals for a perfect measure of investment skill, unaffected by portfolio size.
portfolio_growth.ttwror_note: CF (Cash Flow) = Daily Buys - Daily Sales. On the day you buy, the sub-period runs from your execution price to the close, so that day's move counts.
portfolio_growth.getquin_desc: Measures return on all capital ever deployed. It adds the current value of open positions and all cumulative realized gains, then divides by the total historical buy cost. Realized gains are 'locked in' as permanent return.
portfolio_growth.getquin_formula: (Open value + Cumul. Realized G/L) / Total Invested − 1
portfolio_growth.getquin_note: Unlike TTWROR, this method is affected by the size and timing of contributions, but matches the way apps like Getquin present performance to end users.
portfolio_growth.incomplete_kpi_tooltip: This percentage is an estimate: some asset history is missing, and the calculation values it at 0 across the whole series. Reload in a few seconds to complete it.
portfolio_growth.missing_history: Market data missing for {{count}} asset(s) ({{tickers}}). They count as 0 in the calculation, so this percentage is incomplete — reload in a few minutes.
portfolio_growth.benchmark_only_twr: The benchmark only applies to TTWROR: ROI depends on when you added money, and an index has no contributions.
portfolio_growth.total_return_tooltip: Total gain (unrealised + realised + dividends − fees) over all the capital you have deployed. It is not the ROI the line draws, which only measures open positions.
portfolio_growth.roi_only_all: ROI can only be read over the full range (ALL): over a stretch it measures how much it changed, not what you earned. Use TTWROR.
